_comment: What each trail organisation publishes, data type by data type, as an audit found it on 2026-10-01 for #1793 (Rebuild the data platform as dlt → dbt: seven contracted marts, a monthly refresh, published docs, and lighter phone downloads). One row per organisation × data type: the 173 rows of trail_orgs.json, 92 proposed slugs for the stewards trail_candidates.json names (93 of its 95 new stewards; two Maricopa rows are one department), and two USFS units carrying candidate trails, kept as scoped usfs rows. THIS FILE DECIDES NOTHING ON ITS OWN. It does not load, register or publish anything, and no code reads it. It is the reviewed input that phase 1 writes the pipeline/extract/<club>/ files from: an AVAILABLE_NOT_LOADED row becomes a dlt resource, and a NOT_PUBLISHED or UNKNOWN row becomes that file's dated NOT_AVAILABLE note, quoting the evidence here. Once those files exist this file is retired, so that the notes are the one home (CONTRIBUTING.md). The narrative, the method and every finding that changes another record are in pipeline/ORG_COVERAGE_SURVEY.md. Licences are not settled here: a row being AVAILABLE says the data exists, not that OurHike may publish it.

_statuses.LOADED: A sources.json entry already brings this data type in, from this org or from an upstream row that carries it (the evidence names the key).
_statuses.AVAILABLE_NOT_LOADED: Published and not loaded. Includes pages and PDFs as well as machine-readable layers and feeds, and includes data published about this org's trail by a land manager or partner (the evidence or note says 'via <folder>' where so). It says nothing about licence.
_statuses.NOT_PUBLISHED: Looked for in the places the evidence lists, and not found. Never a guess.
_statuses.UNKNOWN: Could not be told: a bot wall, a login, a key, a timeout, or a site that no longer resolves. Never rounded down to NOT_PUBLISHED.

_grades.measured: The auditor queried it on 2026-10-01 and the count or text can be fetched again.
_grades.reasoned: It follows from something measured, or from a search index rather than the page itself.
_grades.null: The row carried no grade. 87 rows, all UNKNOWN.
_grades.grade_detail: The audit's own grade text where it said more than one word, e.g. 'Measured (ArcGIS); Unknown (website)'.

_method: The audit wrote 28 markdown files, one per batch (scratchpad, not committed): 7 batches for the providers registered in sources.json (b1-b7), 12 for the rest of trail_orgs.json (c1-c12) and 9 for the candidate stewards (c13-c21). A second agent, the skeptic, re-checked each batch and overturned weak verdicts in place; c11 and c12 had no skeptic pass. A persistence pass (decision 21b) then re-worked 202 GIS-shaped NOT_PUBLISHED or UNKNOWN rows with a fixed seven-item checklist (batches p01-p10, q01, r01), and its verdict replaces the audit's. The tables were merged mechanically into rows. Before this file was written, text was trimmed (evidence about 600 characters, notes about 300, cut before a URL rather than through it), and every email address, phone number, personal ArcGIS account name and named private individual was replaced by a description.

_fields.org: A trail_orgs.json slug, or a proposed new slug where candidate is true.
_fields.candidate: true for a steward found through trail_candidates.json and not yet catalogued.
_fields.folds_into: Where the audit recommends no folder of its own: the slug (existing or proposed) whose folder takes this org's data.
_fields.scope: Only on usfs: 'national' for the agency, or the candidate trail and unit a row set describes.
_fields.skeptic: true where the skeptic pass changed the verdict or the evidence.
_fields.persisted: true where the persistence pass set the verdict.
_fields.batch: The audit file the row came from, for tracing it back.
